analytic.title: An Optimized RM Algorithm by Task Affinity On Multi-core Processor

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Scheduling of real-time tasks on a multi-core processor is challenging due to the execution time being a nondeterministic value. Through studying the relationship between task affinity and execution time, we propose an accelerated multi-core real-time scheduling algorithm (RM-) for periodic and dependent real-time tasks on a homogeneous multi-core processor based on acceleration between tasks to obtain a real-time scheduling scheme with less resource utilization. We adopt an acceleration factor matrix to represent the degree of affinity and develop a real-time scheduling model to find the best accelerated pair. The heterogeneous multi-core architectures can execute tasks by sharing their dependent data on L1 Cache. The results demonstrate our approach can loosens the schedulability constraints of RM (maximum improvement of 25%) so that an un-schedulable real-time tasks set on a single-core processor might be schedulable, and for those still hard to be scheduled, could be made schedulable on a multi-core processor.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the demand for high-performance computing in avionics, sea-borne and on-board systems, the related embedded real-time computing systems have become more complicated with higher ability of multi-tasking [1]. Currently, in the practical system, a multi-core processor instead of the single-core processer is applied to improve the performance of hard real-time. But it has a very important issue how to migrate real-time scheduling algorithms from the single processor to the multi-core processor on the premise of ensuring correctness and real-time [2] [3]. Furthermore, on a multi-core processor, it is easy to lead to resource competition, e.g. Cache competition. If the operating system can schedule the dependent tasks by applying some reasonable memory access strategy and scheduling algorithm based on the principle of locality, it can increase the Cache hit due to their sharing resources and improve the processor's performance by reducing data thrashing. This method provides an effective heuristic condition for optimizing the real-time task scheduling on the multi-core processor.

Real-time scheduling in multi-core system is an NP problem and one of the key issues is the schedulability for a given real-time task [4] [5]. This paper proposed a static accelerated real-time scheduling algorithm on a multi-core processor based on the acceleration between tasks for the embedded systems of aviation, healthcare and energy with the characteristics of closed space and relatively fixed number and parameters of tasks. The tasks in these special hard real-time systems will share memory due to their lack of computing resources. It loosens the schedulability constraints of RM algorithm by exploiting the acceleration between the dependent tasks and the heuristic condition of the acceleration effect between the dependent tasks helps the real-time scheduling algorithm convergence much faster. Further, an un-schedulable real-time tasks set on a single-core processor might be schedulable on a multi-core processor. The acceleration refers to the interaction between dependent tasks due to their sharing or competition for the limited resources, when they are executed under the same computing system. In this paper, we use the acceleration as a heuristic condition to optimize the task scheduling strategy and obtain an efficient real-time task scheduling scheme with less resource utilization.

Real-time scheduling in multi-core system has greatly expanded the study of traditional scheduling algorithms. But the researches achieved in the single-core model cannot be applied directly to the multi-core system due to its nondeterministic execution time [6~8]. In 1973, two researchers at NASA's jet propulsion lab, C.Liu and J.Layland first proposed a fixed-priority algorithm Rate Monotonic (RM) and a dynamic priority algorithm Earliest Deadline First (EDF) and gave a sufficient schedulable condition based on resource utilization [9~11]. In 1995, Almut Burchard et. al. improved the upper bounds of the resource utilization of RM and gave a higher value of the minimum upper bounds to expand the range of schedulability. [12] Later, Lehoczky et. al. proposed a sufficient and necessary condition for RM [13]. The [14~16] analysed the schedulability for tasks by calculating the resource utilization of algorithms. [17~20] designed some improved algorithms, e.g. Generalized RM algorithm, Hyperbolic RM algorithm and EDF on multi-core processor, to develop real-time scheduling. Among them, Buttazzo applied mechanics to real-time scheduling to propose a new spring scheduling algorithm. He regraded the concurrent tasks as a series spring system and it improved its recourse utilization by a parameter similar to spring constant.

How to both ensure the real-time performance of the system and make full use of multi-core processor's computing power has become the key problem in the study of real-time scheduling. Therefore, this paper does some research on the real-time schedulability analysis. And on the basis of RM algorithm and the characteristic of sharing Cache in the multi-core architecture, we proposes an improved real-time scheduling algorithm, RM-λ by introducing the tasks' acceleration and focuses on the improvement of real-time scheduling condition in the multi-core system. At present, the methods, to obtain an efficient real-time scheduling scheme by making the most of task affinity to minimize the resource utilization, applied in this paper are quite few.
The main contributions of this paper include:

We propose a concept of Acceleration Factor: The acceleration factor of each task obtained through the practical testing on a multi-core platform, is used as a heuristic condition for analyzing the schedulability of the real-time tasks to accelerate the scheduling algorithm's convergence speed. We can analyse the affinity between tasks according to the acceleration factor and it is an effective method for real-time scheduling in multi-core system.

We propose a real-time scheduling model AMRSM for multi-core system: It improves the scheduling model and scheduling constraint of RM based on two characteristics of multi-core system: sharing Cache and acceleration between tasks.

We design a static accelerated scheduling algorithm RM-λ based on RM. It can schedule the real-time tasks by minimizing the resource utilization based on the acceleration between tasks. It can get a looser real-time scheduling condition than RM so that an un-schedulable real time task set on a single-core processor might be schedulable on a multi-core processor.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. The real-time scheduling multi-core model and related definitions are presented in Section 2. A motivational example is presented in Section 3 to illustrate the basic ideas of RM-λ algorithm. The multicore scheduling model is described in Section 4. The accelerated real-time scheduling algorithm RM-λ is presented in Section 5. The experimental results are presented in Section 6. Section 7 concludes the paper.

div.head: II. BASIC MODEL
div.p: In this section, we introduce the Homogeneous Multi-Core system (HMC) architecture, followed by the Accelerated Multi-core Real-time Scheduling Model (AMRSM), the Accelerated Real-time Tasks Set (ARTS) and other definitions.

div.head: A. Hardware Model
div.p: The target architecture HMC is shown in Fig. 1. Formally, the hardware model is a set of m homogeneous cores { , ,…, ,…, } and each core is equipped with a local L1 Cache and a shared L2 Cache. The cores access data on L2 Cache through Bus. The capacity of L1 cache and L2 cache is very limited, so that the takes will share resources. If two tasks share their data in the same L1 Cache, we call it Serial Acceleration. The overhead of Serial Acceleration is small and it has the most acceleration effect. If two tasks share their data on L2 Cache, we call it Parallel Acceleration. It incurs more latency and less acceleration effect than serial acceleration. In this paper, we mainly focused on Serial Acceleration to get better task affinity. The more data the tasks share on L1 Cache, the more execution time can be saved and the more efficient scheduling scheme can be obtained.

div.p: In this section, we propose a static accelerated real-time scheduling algorithm (RM-λ) to find a real-time scheduling scheme with less resource utilization on the condition that each real-time periodic task can be completed within its deadline in a given AMRSM model the ARTS tasks set. Algorithm 5.1 shows the RM-λ algorithm. Initially, we build a matrix TA[ ][ ] to record each task's acceleration factor and TA[ ][ ] represents the λ (defined in Section 3). The variables S( ), C i (S) and GS are used to record the series acceleration of task , the already assigned tasks on the core and the global acceleration factor sequence, respectively. And α( ) is a function which is used to look for a task's largest acceleration factor in Acceleration Factor Matrix and Li(n) is the least recourse utilization of core .

The RM-λ algorithm tries to find the best acceleration pair according to the task affinity and obtained an optimal tasks assignment method and scheduling strategy to make the sum of each core's resource utilization as little as possible. From line 3 to line 6, the algorithm calculates the acceleration factor for each task and obtains GS by sorting them in ascending order. From line 7 to line 12, the algorithm divides the tasks into several sequences according to the order of the task affinity and the number of the scheduling sequence on each core is limited by the scheduling condition of RM. From line 13 to line 17, the execution order on each core is decided by the order of the acceleration factor. From line 18 to the end is used to verify whether the optimal task scheduling we found can be scheduled in multi-core system.

div.head: VI. EXPERIMENTS
div.p: Experimental results are presented in this section. We selected 5 jobs for each task which is defined in Table I to complete the experiment and the total number of jobs is 30. Our main method is to enumerate all the tasks assignments and measure their execution time, respectively. Then, the effectiveness of the RM-λ algorithm is proved according to the statistical data.

div.head: A. Experiment Environment
div.p: In our experiment, we use a multi-core platform Beehive to execute all the real-time tasks. Beehive is designed by Microsoft Research and it has 13 homogeneous cores and 3 of special cores. Each homogeneous core has its local L1 cache and can access data from memory through L2 Cache. The test data of TSP are got from the TSPLIB benchmark.

div.head: B. Test Task Execution Time
div.p: For any combination of tasks, e.g.{<1,4>,<2,8>,<3,5>}, their execution sequence of 30 jobs is <1,4>,<2,8>,<3,5><1,4>,<2,8>,<3,5>,…, which are executed periodically 5 times and their total execution time are recorded. Table VI shows a part of these data.

According to the test, the smallest execution time is 25.03s which is obtained by executing the tasks scheduling, P( ) = { , , } and P( ) = { , , } and the largest execution time is 29.67s which is obtained by executing the tasks scheduling, P( ) = { , , } and P( ) = { , , }. The average execution time of the combinations including task 5 and task 4 is 26.96s, the average execution time of the combinations including task 1 and task 5 is 28.63s and the average execution time of all the other tasks assignments is 28.38s.

Compared with the execution time of all the other scheduling, the execution time of optimal tasks scheduling is saved by (28.38-25.03)/ 28.38 =11.8%. Compared with the longest execution time, the execution time of optimal tasks scheduling is saved by (29.67-25.03)/ 29.67 = 15.6%. These experiments verify it is better to assign the tasks with high affinity to the same core to minimize the resource utilization, which is accordance with the conclusion we draw in Section 4. E.g. task 5 should be executed concurrently with task 4 due to they have the largest acceleration factor.

div.head: C. Test Task Completion Rates
div.p: In this paper, our purpose is to schedule a set of real-time periodic and dependent tasks with as less recourse utilization as possible. When we obtained the real-time scheduling scheme, we test its task completion rates. The clock frequency of Beehive platform is 150 Mclocks and the cycle of each task is 1.5s. In our test, the utilization of a core for each task can be calculated by using the formula: E( )/150, where E( ) represents the completion probability of task , which is shown in Fig. 3. From the experiment, we obtained the tasks completion rates on three cores is 38% and the tasks completion rates on two cores is 25%. Task Comlecation Rate cores will both improve the calculation speed and the task completion rate. When the utilization rate of CPU is very high, the task completion rate on Two Cores is almost 1.5 times of that on Three Cores. And if the tasks have the acceleration between each other, increasing the number of cores will improve the schedulability.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, we propose a static accelerated real-time scheduling algorithm (RM-λ) for periodic and dependent tasks on a homogeneous multi-core processor to minimize the resource utilization based on acceleration between tasks. We build an accelerated multi-core real-time scheduling model and an acceleration factor matrix to obtain a real-time scheduling scheme to make each tasks executed within its deadline. The experimental results show that RM-λ algorithm is efficient and an un-schedulable real-time tasks set on a single-core processor might be schedulable, and for those still hard to be scheduled, could be made schedulable on a multi-core processor.
